answers.U1-S1: Seeing flamingos for the first time at age six, on a walk to the river with his brothers, was more amazing than any time he saw them later.
answers.U1-S2: He was young and scared easily. He agreed to go first and only got nervous about the cattle afterward, so his brother had to promise to avoid them.
answers.U1-S3: To show the walk was long and tiring for a little boy. Because the walk was so long, they ended up wandering into thistles and tall grass.
answers.U1-S4: seriously, slowly and calmly, like they were in a ceremony
answers.U1-S5: Because he was so amazed staring at it, the bird noticed and showed off its wings, and he saw they were bright crimson.
answers.U1-S6: The birds were rare there. They had never seen them before, which is why the river overflowed and brought them, so it was a special sighting.
answers.U1-S7: Because it was tall, white and rose, with glorious crimson wings, and seemed so beautiful and graceful to him, almost heavenly.
answers.U1-S8: Because seeing them hundreds of times made them ordinary to him, his first sighting seemed less special, so later views couldn't match how he felt then.
answers.U1-S9: It jumps ahead to his later life and compares many later sightings to the first one, showing the first one stayed the best.
answers.U1-S10: Fond and nostalgic; he still treasures the memory and thinks it was the most delightful moment.
